essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances while letting some small nonpolar molecules pass.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.

activities.label: Membrane model
activities.title: Phospholipids and movement
activities.body: Study the membrane model. Then get ready to explain it in your own words.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because their hydrophobic interior blocks many polar or charged substances while letting some small nonpolar molecules pass.

activities.label: Own words check
activities.title: Why some substances cross
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain why some substances cross the membrane more easily than others.
activities.correctAnswer: The hydrophobic interior of the phospholipid bilayer blocks many polar or charged substances, so only some small nonpolar substances pass easily.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links membrane structure to movement across it. If needed, add that the bilayer’s interior is hydrophobic and that this creates selective permeability.

activities.label: Fix the rule
activities.title: Passive or active transport
activities.body: Correct the rule you used before. State the transport type and what makes it that type.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing passive transport with active transport by treating energy use as optional or by ignoring concentration gradients.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: The key difference is energy and gradient direction. If your first answer blurred them, repair it by naming both parts clearly.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Transport in plain language
activities.body: Explain passive and active transport again in your own words.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport goes down the concentration gradient without energy, and active transport goes against the gradient using energy.
activities.feedback: A strong response keeps the two transport types distinct and includes energy use plus gradient direction.

activities.label: Classify one example
activities.title: Choose the transport type
activities.body: Pick the best answer for this case and submit it.
choices: A substance moves from high concentration to low concentration without energy. This is passive transport.
A substance moves from low concentration to high concentration without energy. This is passive transport.
A substance moves from high concentration to low concentration using energy. This is active transport.
A substance moves only through the membrane because it is large. This is active transport.
activities.correctAnswer: A substance moves from high concentration to low concentration without energy. This is passive transport.
activities.feedback: Passive transport moves down a gradient without energy. Active transport is the one that requires energy, usually to move against the gradient.

activities.label: Wrap up
activities.title: What is now clear?
activities.body: Name one thing you can now explain without help.
